Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 152 S. 09 20111 MR. PERTER JD SMITH MBA Compound Bagumbong 1421 Caloocan City North Dear Mr. Smith: 2010 This has reference to your earlier letter asking this Department's advice on the following queries which we quoted in toto: "1) In the circumstance that official property, financial and records are not turned-over and cannot be located in the barangay hall, what proceedings have to be initiated and by whom to obtain the return of the said illegally removed property, financial and records to their proper place in the barangay hall? e) What is the legal status of the said property, financial and records during their illegal absence from their proper place? S) What will the legal status of the said illegally removed property, financial and records be once they have been retrieved in whole or in part and perhaps having been tampered? 4) What proceedings can be initiated against the offending party/parties? 5) What proceeding can be initiated against City/MunicipaI Mayors who fail to comply with Section 32 of the Local Government CodeP With regard to your first up to fourth queries, we regret to inform you that we cannot properly advise you on the said issues. In your letter, it was not sufficiently established as to how the property, financial and records were removed from their proper place in the barangay hall or that these properties and records were indeed illegally removed therein by the former Punong Barangay and not some other persons for some other causes. May we note that your allegation that these properties and records were not handed over to the incumbent Punong Barangay by its predecessor was based only on "reasonable assumption". Anent your fifth query, Section 32 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides and we quote: "SECTION 32. City and Municipal Supervision over Their Respective Barangays.— The city or municipality, through the city

or municipal mayor concerned, shall exercise general supervision over component barangays to ensure that said barangays act within the scope of their prescribed powers and fimctions. The failure of the City or Municipal Mayor to comply with the aforequoted provision of the Code may warrant for the filing of an administrative case for dereliction or neglect of duty against him before the proper forum. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, . JESUS B. DOQUEIV Director III A Ls/17 Copy furnished: Regional Director Renato L. Brion DILG-NCR
